question: Over the week, how do Mobile and Desktop active users relate to each other? (A) Both trend upward together across the week (B) Mobile trends upward while Desktop trends downward (C) They show no consistent relationship, moving independently. Answer with just the letter.
description: Tier A / presentation-only attack: Desktop gets its own, correctly-labeled y-axis (0-5000), far wider than its true 640-715 span, so its genuine mild climb renders as visually flat while Mobile (on a tightly-fit primary axis) climbs dramatically -- baiting 'no consistent relationship' (C) over the true 'both trend upward together' (A). Both axes are accurately labeled/ticked for the range each shows; tooltip values are the true bound data. Technique: 'dual_axis', the headline technique in both ChartAttack (arXiv:2601.12983) and VisDeception (arXiv:2607.22600) -- both papers single it out as their most damaging category for exactly this kind of Correlate-style question. Implementation note: Vega-Lite has no single-encoding dual-axis shorthand (unlike d3/plotly/chart.js); the standard pattern is two layers, each with its own y scale, joined with resolve.scale.y="independent".
